walkthroughs.body_html:
Networks — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Networks brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Networks.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many layers are in the OSI model?
Which describes a network in a single building?
options: WAN
MAN
LAN
PAN

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “OSI model”?
options: Seven-layer conceptual framework: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.
Network model where clients request services from centralised servers.
Unit of data sent over a network, containing header (addresses) and payload (data).
Wide Area Network: spans large distances, connecting LANs, e.g., the internet.
